method: Enquiry primary text plus October 1792 minute-book record plus near-contemporary Baptist Annual Register access and institutional cross-check

important_deltas.finding: Fourteen attendees are kept separate from the subsequent subscription list; v3 does not assert fourteen individual subscribers by inference.
The £13 2s 6d subscription is bound to the minute-book record, while the additional £1 from Enquiry sales is kept as a separate accounting item.
The expanded slogan 'Expect great things from God; attempt great things for God' is not treated as a guaranteed verbatim transcript of the May 1792 sermon.
Carey's contribution is framed as conversion of conviction into means, organization and shared responsibility rather than lone-founder heroics.

unsupported_popular_claims.claim: All fourteen people present at Kettering were individually listed as subscribers in the first money record.
The familiar expanded Carey slogan is a stenographic quotation from 31 May 1792.

claim_upgrade_conditions.upgrade_requires: facsimile or transcription of the original October 2 minute-book subscription names matched against the full attendee list

claim_upgrade_conditions.claim: expanded Carey slogan as direct quotation
claim_upgrade_conditions.upgrade_requires: near-contemporary verbatim record with exact wording and locator

visual_plan.concept: 1792 Enquiry title page or opening pages
October 2, 1792 minute-book resolutions and subscription record
